subject: SLA: production 5xx/429 surge — capacity hit & autoscale lag (OpenCare)
messages:
From: Matt Healy <matt.healy@opencare.ai>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Production: sudden 5xx/429 errors since 09:00 UTC

Rachel —

We started seeing a spike of 5xx and 429s across our inference calls starting ~09:00 UTC (about 30 minutes ago). Latency jumped from ~120ms to >2s before timeouts. Retries on our side made things worse — we saw a retry storm and a large backlog. This is impacting the inference-based triage flow for our ambulatory product.

Attached is a small snippet from our client logs showing repeated 503/429 responses and client-side backoffs. Can you confirm whether this is an OpenCare-side throttling or something on Redwood? Our SLA window is currently in the red and we need an immediate workaround; turning off retries is a short-term option but will increase user-visible failures.

Please escalate to whoever is needed — this is affecting our active users and a scheduled demo in 90 minutes.

— Matt
Matt Healy
Head of Product, OpenCare
attachments: support_log_snippet.txt
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>

Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-15T09:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden 5xx/429 errors since 09:00 UTC

Matt —

Thanks for the heads-up and the log snippet. We see these signals in our dashboards too and I have looped in CS (Neha) and on-call infra (Sean) to investigate immediately. Quick answers / immediate steps we can take while we triage:

- Can you temporarily disable automated retries for the affected endpoints? That will reduce pressure on the queue while we diagnose.
- We can enable an emergency per-account throttle on our side to limit request bursts (low-friction, reversible). Please confirm if we have permission to apply that.
- If acceptable, we can failover the workload to a smaller, compatible model variant (a single API flag) to keep tail latency down. That reduces quality but preserves availability.

We are opening a high-priority incident (INC-20261115-71) and will update every 30 minutes until resolved. I will share a short executive summary and next steps once we have a remediation path.

— Rachel
Rachel Kim

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-11-15T09:27:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Production: sudden 5xx/429 errors — initial observations

Forwarding Matt's note + our initial telemetry. Key points from infra metrics:

- Host pool (us-west-1-hosted) showed a rapid increase in queued requests starting 08:55 UTC; GPU memory usage hit >94% on three replicas by 09:05 UTC.
- Autoscaler reacted but with ~90s lag to spin new replicas (cold-start + model load), during which many requests timed out with 5xx.
- Client retry behaviour created a retry-amplification loop in the request queue.
- A subset of requests had unusually long sequences and KV cache growth which amplified per-request memory.

Attached: pool_scaling-timeline.csv (timeline of replica counts, memory, queued depth) and a small grep of request latencies.

Proposed immediate mitigations (short-term):
1) Apply per-account burst throttle for OpenCare to 40rps (need Rachel to confirm).
2) Temporarily enable the compatible smaller model variant (reduces RAM footprint).
3) If OpenCare agrees, bring them briefly onto our dedicated reserve (if they have it) or use reserved burst capacity to avoid cold-starts.

Longer-term actions to avoid recurrence: tighten autoscaler thresholds for this workload pattern; pre-warm model caches for accounts with predictable morning peaks; add a circuit-breaker that returns 429 early instead of letting requests queue to OOM.

— Neha
Neha Kapoor
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
attachments: pool_scaling-timeline.csv

Date: 2026-11-15T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production: sudden 5xx/429 errors — infra notes + immediate action

Quick update from on-call infra: we validated Neha's summary. Root cause summary: autoscale cold-start lag combined with heavy KV-cache growth per request caused sustained GPU memory pressure and replica instability. The autoscaler is conservative for this pool to prioritize model stability, which increased the reaction time under a sudden burst.

Immediate actions executed (09:40–10:00 UTC):
- Applied temporary per-account throttling (OpenCare) to 40rps at the routing layer.
- Increased the autoscaler target for the host pool and initiated two warm replicas from reserve (reduced cold-start time).
- Enabled fallback to the smaller model variant for OpenCare's traffic (flagged on their account) to reduce memory per-inference.
- Cleared the request queue and monitored for 20m; 5xx rate dropped from ~18% to <1% and 429s reduced significantly.

We attached a dashboard screen capture (dashboard_5xx_spike.png) with the before/after. Next steps: full RCA and a postmortem outlining tuning for autoscaler thresholds and introducing an account-level circuit breaker. We'll also document suggested client retry best-practices (jittered exponential backoff + hard cap).

— Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
attachments: dashboard_5xx_spike.png

Subject: Incident update & executive summary (OpenCare) — next steps + credit

Matt —

Follow-up and summary after the mitigation yesterday:

What happened (brief): a sudden morning burst caused GPU memory pressure in the hosted pool while autoscaler responded with ~90s lag. Client retries amplified the queue, producing elevated 5xx/429 rates during the cold-start window.

What we did (actions taken):
- Applied temporary per-account throttling to avoid queue amplification.
- Increased warm replica targets and used reserve capacity to shorten cold-start time.
- Enabled a smaller model variant to reduce per-request memory and recovered tail latency.
- Opened high-priority incident INC-20261115-71; engineering will produce a detailed RCA within 48 hours.

Impact: OpenCare saw degraded SLA for ~18 minutes with user-facing effects during a scheduled demo slot. 5xx rate peaked ~18% and then dropped to <1% after remediation.

Proposed customer remediation: we will issue a one-week pro-rated credit for impacted usage and a technical review session with our infra leads (Sean) and your engineering team to discuss changes to autoscaler tuning and retry strategies.

Requested approvals / asks from you:
1) Permission to keep the smaller model flag active for the next 24 hours while we validate stability.
2) Approval for the one-week pro-rated credit (I'll process through finance once you confirm).

Next steps from Redwood: full RCA and postmortem (by 2026-11-18), implementation plan to pre-warm caches for predictable peaks, and a recommended client retry policy doc.

Sorry for the disruption — we know this is not acceptable and we'll follow through on fixes and compensation. If you'd like an immediate call, I can get Sean and Neha on with me.

— Rachel
